Thanks for the details — here is the concise breakdown of our current billing logic (production SKU behavior, as of our November pricing stack). I'll include a worked example below.

1) Cache / KV hits
- KV/prefix cache: we do not bill tokens for bytes fully satisfied from a read-only KV prefix cache. Practically, the billed prompt token count is the length of the *non-cached* prompt segment submitted to the model. If a request contains a 120-token prefix and a 30-token user message, and the 120-token prefix is fully satisfied from KV, the billed prompt tokens are 30.
- Note: some legacy integrations (older SDKs or proxying) may materialize the full prompt server-side before sending; in those cases the request will appear to the runtime as the full padded prompt and will be billed accordingly. We can check your request IDs to verify whether materialization happened.

2) Multi-model fallbacks
- Billing is computed per request by summing the tokens consumed by each model execution during that request, then applying request-level rounding and minimums. We do NOT round each model execution separately then sum (that prevents over-rounding).

3) Rounding & minimums
- Basic unit: 1 token (we round any fractional tokens up to the next whole token).
- Request-level minimum: 10 tokens for streaming responses on the legacy "starter" SKU to cover steady-state overhead. Newer committed SKUs (what most enterprise accounts are moved to) have no per-request floor — they bill exact token counts after rounding.
- Aggregation rule: tokens_total = sum(tokens_by_model) -> tokens_billed = max(tokens_total_rounded, sku_minimum)

4) Discounts & credits
- Discounts (committed % discounts) are applied to the billed token amount after rounding and minimum rules. Invoice-level credits (one-time promotional credits or PO credits) are applied after discounting as invoice adjustments. Trial credits in the billing system are allocated before invoice adjustments but after discount application — this can make a line-item appear zero even if a discount exists.

Worked example (your scenario simplified):
- A single request uses Model A for prompt (20.6 tokens billed after internal tokenization) then falls back to Model B to finish and uses 45.3 tokens.
- sum raw tokens = 20.6 + 45.3 = 65.9 -> round up = 66 tokens.
- SKU minimum = 10 (legacy) -> billed = max(66,10) = 66.
- Apply 10% committed discount -> charged tokens' value = price_per_token * 66 * 0.9.
- Invoice-level $25k credit applied at invoice close, not at per-request line item.

Notes specific to your export: I reviewed the request IDs you flagged. Two of them show server-side prompt materialization (SDK v0.9.1) — that explains why the prefix appears billed on those rows. We have a migration note to avoid that but your account still had some older clients. I'll attach the flagged request ids in a follow-up if you want to reconcile line-by-line.

If you want us to do the math and propose a one-time adjustment for the disputed invoice, we can run a reconciliation. Given the deal and your committed discount, I recommend we:
- Run a line-by-line reconciliation for the rows you flagged (we'll check SDK versions and materialization).
- If materialization is the cause, we propose a one-time invoice credit equal to the billed prompt tokens that should have been excluded, net of your 10% discount.

Happy to run this — give the greenlight and we'll start.

—Karthik

- For fallbacks we aggregate raw tokens across both models, then round to whole tokens once, then apply any SKU minimum.
- Committed discounts are applied after rounding; invoice credits are applied last.
